gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Epoch's 12V 105Ah Essential Heated starts its heater from as little as 0.5 A of charge current. That is 1/8 of the more than 4 A Renogy's heater needs (0.5 ÷ 4) and 1/20 of the 10 A LiTime needs in Regular mode (0.5 ÷ 10). It also packs 60.8 Wh per lb (1,344 Wh ÷ 22.1 lb), against 47.6 Wh/lb for the best heated model BatteryTrail lists.
standout_why: I compared against BatteryTrail's spec database (cited), CompareFoundry's cold-charging guide (cited) and BoondockMaps' best-lithium list (cited). BatteryTrail works out $/Wh and Wh/lb for its heated models (Battle Born, Renogy Pro, SOK, Dakota, CHINS) but leaves out the Epoch and LiTime heated models and publishes no heater draw. CompareFoundry gives LiTime's 10 A and Renogy's 4 A charger minimums but nothing for Epoch, and no prices, Wh or weights. BoondockMaps lists Epoch at $450-500 and 22.1 lb but gives no heater trigger current and no Wh per lb. None of them puts the charge current each heater needs side by side. I could not open Gear Ranking (TLS certificate error), so I can't rule out that it has this.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's Epoch pick for one specific reason. A 0.5 A trickle, such as a small solar panel on a short winter day, is enough to start the Epoch's heater. The same trickle never reaches Renogy's 4 A or LiTime's 10 A threshold, so those batteries stay too cold to charge. Epoch is also the densest heated 12V 100Ah-class battery I could source (60.8 Wh/lb). On price per Wh it costs $0.41 at $549, which is more than Renogy Pro's $0.45 at BatteryTrail's $579.99 is not; Renogy is dearer, so the Epoch is cheaper per Wh than Renogy and Battle Born but not the cheapest heated battery overall (SOK at $0.29 on BatteryTrail).
